title: SDK sample kit & staged migration playbook for streaming + structured output + function-calling
creator: Asha Mehta
body:
Executive summary:
We need a tightly coordinated sample kit and staged migration playbook for SDK v2.1 to accompany the API surface release that enables streaming, structured output (schema validation + examples), and function calling improvements. The outcome is a set of curated samples, a migration helper script for customers on older SDKs, localized README snippets, release notes, and a cross-team rollout runbook for canary -> ramp -> GA with telemetry gates and automated rollback triggers.

Goals:
- Provide 10 canonical end-to-end samples (Node/Python/Go) demonstrating streaming, structured outputs (JSON Schema and proto examples), and function calling patterns (sync and streaming).
- Ship a migration shim + compatibility tests so customers can upgrade with minimal code changes.
- Ensure release notes include explicit migration steps, a deprecation timeline for old params, and links to interactive sandboxes.
- Coordinate canary rollout with Eng autoscaling and Console feature flags; ensure telemetry and error budgets are monitored.

Scope (in):
- Sample code for the three SDKs (Node, Python, Go).
- Migration script repository (CLI: redwood-sdk-migrate) that rewrites common call shapes and flags breaking changes.
- Release notes draft and localized README snippets for en/fr/de.
- Canary rollout plan and telemetry gating criteria.

Out of scope:
- Full refactor of existing SDKs to new internals (this is handled in ENG-20312).
- Long-term deprecation automation for downstream SDKs (future epic).

Milestones and timeline:
- 2026-03-03: Finalize sample list and acceptance criteria (DONE).
- 2026-03-07: Eng completes compat test harness and first-pass migration shim (ENG-19876 blocking, in review).
- 2026-03-10: Docs team publishes staging pages for sample snippets (staging.redwood.dev/sdk).
- 2026-03-13: Cross-team runbook reviewed and signoffs obtained from Eng, Design, Security.
- 2026-03-17: Canary rollout starts (5% traffic), telemetry gates enabled.
- 2026-03-20: Planned GA (subject to telemetry).

Acceptance criteria:
- All 10 samples pass CI smoke and compatibility matrix + E2E against runtime-1.18.
- Migration CLI rewrites >= 80% of observed legacy call patterns in our internal corpus without manual edits.
- Release notes include explicit migration code snippets, links to interactive sandboxes, and a deprecation schedule.
- Console feature flag exists for staged rollout with rollback endpoints instrumented.

Rollout strategy and gating:
- Canary 5% (48h): monitor error rate (<= 0.5% absolute increase), median p99 latency (<= +30ms), and token cost changes (+/- 5% acceptable).
- Ramp 25% (72h): require no regressions in model quality metrics on representative eval sets; auto-abort if quality drops by >2% on key prompts.
- GA: 100% after 7 days stable.
- Rollback: automated if any gate fails OR manual rollback via Console if customer-impacting regression detected.

Migration notes (high level):
- function calling: major changes are optional 'streaming-compatible' handlers and new call signature for named outputs. Migration shim rewrites handler signatures and attaches streaming callbacks.
- structured output: schema validation is opt-in by default; migration adds a compatibility flag --enable-schema to adopt strict parsing.
- streaming: default chunk framing changed slightly; the shim includes a framing shim that can be toggled off.

Sample kit contents:
- /samples/node/streaming-function-calls/README.md + runnable app and test harness.
- /samples/python/structured-output-schema/ with JSON schema examples and validation helpers.
- /samples/go/migration-cli/ usage examples and Dockerfile for local testing.
- interactive playground links embedded in READMEs pointing at the staging playground.

Docs + release notes coordination:
- Primary release note author: Diego Alvarez.
- PR for release notes must include: short 'What changed' bullets, 'Migration steps' section with copy-paste snippets, 'Known issues' table, and link to migration CLI.
- Localization: EN -> FR/DE by Docs localization team; priority for migration steps and example snippets.

Owners & responsibilities:
- PM (Asha): owns rollout cadence, signoffs, customer comms.
- Eng (owner: Priya Kapoor): compat tests, migration shim, runtime compatibility.
- Docs (owner: Diego): samples, release notes, localized snippets.
- Design (owner: Mikael Chen): sample UX for interactive playground and screenshots for release notes.
- QA (owner: Lena Ortiz): test matrix and final smoke.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: migration CLI fails on edge case customer patterns -> mitigation: create a 'manual review' report showing rewrites and diffs, include quick rollback instructions.
- Risk: streaming changes increase p99 latency -> mitigation: throttled canary + kernel-level telemetry hooks (ENG-20488).

Customer comms and deprecation timeline:
- Pre-GA: blog preview + developer webinar (date TBD).
- GA: release announcement, migration guide, sample kit repo announcement.
- Deprecation: mark legacy parameters deprecated on GA, begin 6-month deprecation countdown with automated warnings in Console and SDK logs.

Acceptance test matrix (high level):
- SDK Node/Python/Go: unit, compat, and e2e for each sample.
- Backend runtime: load test with 10k concurrent tokens, memory and KV cache correctness.
- Console: feature flag behavior and rollback test.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Merge sample PRs to staging and attach links to release notes PR.
2) Finalize migration CLI README and release a 0.1.0 tagged artifact.
3) Schedule customer webinar and create support playbook for migration requests.

Notes: emphasize migration-first messaging in release notes (how-to, pitfalls, and one-liners for support teams).

qa_plan: QA plan (summary): run CI across Node/Python/Go samples; execute migration CLI against internal corpus (1000 real call traces); run load test at 1x, 5x, 10x baseline traffic for p50/p95/p99; manual exploratory on interactive playground; final signoff meeting where QA owner (Lena) approves GA. Failure modes require immediate rollback and post-mortem within 72 hours.
release_notes_draft:
What's new:
- Streaming updates: lower-latency chunk framing and streaming-compatible function-calling handlers.
- Structured output: opt-in JSON Schema validation with examples for common schemas.
- Function calling: improved handler ergonomics and streaming handler support.

Migration notes (short):
- Install redwood-sdk-migrate and run: redwood-sdk-migrate rewrite --path ./src --preview to preview rewrites.
- Add --enable-schema to enable strict structured output parsing.
- If you rely on legacy framing, set REDWOOD_STREAM_FRAMING=legacy until you migrate.

Breaking changes:
- function handler signature updated for streaming use-cases (see migration CLI output for automated fixes).

Known issues:
- Two edge-case streaming patterns may require manual handler adjustments (tracked ENG-20488).

Links:
- Migration CLI: github.com/redwood/redwood-sdk-migrate
- Samples: github.com/redwood/samples/tree/sdk-2.1
- Interactive sandbox: staging.redwood.dev/sdk
